---
title: "How do I explore whether a time series has a stable mean over time?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I explore whether a time series has a stable mean over time?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Plot the measurements against time.

2. Compare early and late windows of similar length.

3. Inspect whether trend or changing spread contradicts a stable process.

## Runnable example

```{r}
set.seed(3)
stable <- rnorm(80,mean=8,sd=2)
trending <- stable + seq(0,12,length.out=80)
op <- par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(stable,type="l",col="#3F78A8",ylab="Value",
     main="Simulated stable process")
plot(trending,type="l",col="#A35E20",ylab="Value",
     main="Same noise with increasing trend")
par(op)
print(c(mean(stable[1:40]),mean(stable[41:80])))
print(c(mean(trending[1:40]),mean(trending[41:80])))
```

## Interpret the result

The second series has an imposed upward trend and therefore does not have a constant mean. A stable-looking sample does not by itself prove stationarity.

## Check before applying to real data

Two window means and a plot are preliminary checks, not proof of stationarity. Also consider variance and serial dependence.
